newsitem.title: USA: Steady U.S. rate becalms emerging market debt.
newsitem.headline: Steady U.S. rate becalms emerging market debt.

text.p: A subdued LDC debt market took in stride the widely expected decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve policy makers to leave key rates unchanged.

Spreads of emerging debt over U.S. Treasuries were unchanged to slightly tigher prior to the rate announcement and trades were few afterwards, said traders, noting the hesitant tone in the Treasury stymied any signifcant moves.
Looking ahead, analysts expected the emerging debt prices to rise at a slower pace as the spectacular contraction of spreads in the first half of the year became hard to duplicate.
"People will protect what they have," said Kip Allardt, emerging market debt strategist at CS First Boston, expecting a more cautious trading environment ahead.
Mexico's robust 8.8 percent growth in the second quarter reported on Monday took the breath away of economists, many of whom were busy revising their forecastes, he said.
The macroeconomic picture in other major Latin American countries are healthy and capital inflows steady.
Even worries about Brazil's currency stability in the aftermath of the Thai baht devaluation had so far produced no drastic change in investors' sentiment, Allardt said.
